# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_015_page_001.jpg

---

1 But you, our God — you are kind and faithful, slow to anger, and you govern everything with mercy.

2 Even when we sin, we are still yours, for we know your power; and knowing that we belong to you, we will not sin.

3 To know you is the fullness of righteousness; to know your power is the very root of immortality.

4 No cunning scheme of men has led us astray, and no painter's empty labour — some form smeared over with a muddle of colours,

5 the sight of which stirs up a fool's desire, so that he aches for the lifeless shape of a painted image.

6 Those who make such things, who want them, who bow down to them — they are lovers of evil and deserve every empty hope they have.

7 A potter works hard, kneading soft earth, shaping vessel after vessel for our daily use. From the very same clay he makes both pots for honourable purposes and pots for the opposite — and it is entirely the potter's decision how each will be used.

8 With wearisome effort he shapes from that same clay a worthless god — this man who was himself shaped from earth a little while ago, and who will return to that same earth before long, when the debt of his life is called due.

9 But none of that troubles him — not the strain of the work, not the shortness of his days. He tries to keep up with the goldsmith, to match the silversmith, he copies the bronze-worker, and he takes it as an achievement that he turns out fakes.

10 His heart is ash. His hope is worth less than dirt. His life is more contemptible than clay,

11 because he never knew the one who formed him, who breathed a living soul into him and blew the breath of life through him.

12 He treats our whole existence as a children's game and our life as a market stall for making money. He says you have to profit wherever you can — even from wickedness.

13 Above all sinners, this man knows he is doing wrong — the one who takes earthly mud and fashions it into flimsy pots and graven idols.

14 But more foolish than all of them, and more pitiable than even a newborn child, are the enemies of your people who enslaved them —

15 those who counted all the idols of the nations as gods. Things that cannot open their eyes to see, cannot flare their nostrils to breathe, cannot cup their ears to hear, cannot stretch out fingers to touch — and with feet that have never once walked.

16 A man made them. A creature whose own breath is borrowed shaped them. No human being can mold into existence a god equal to himself.

17 He is mortal, and the thing he makes with his lawless hands is dead. He is better than his own gods, at least — because he has lived, and they never have.

18 And to top it all, they worship the most revolting creatures alive. Measured by sheer stupidity, these Egyptian worshippers are worse than any others —

19 and the creatures they adore are not even beautiful enough to inspire desire. They are creatures passed over by God's blessing and praise alike.
